notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: Friday has no EGX session, so the latest close is Thursday 29 October (EGX30 49,596.14). The CBE's 100 bp hike is announced after Thursday's close, so Sunday 1 November is the market's first session to price it. Brent is Thursday's settlement. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Thursday's debt flows (bills and bonds), the budget's oil-price assumption, Egypt's October inflation figure (AFP puts it at about 14% while October data are not yet scheduled, so it is not used), a settlement price for gold (quotes from different times disagree), and any 364-day T-bill auction after the hike. Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday flow figures (foreign net buying of EGP 42.259 bn and Arab EGP 9.820 bn) disagree with Youm7 and Cairo Mubasher (EGP 29.2 bn and EGP 2.24 bn), so the chart uses the two sources that agree.
notes.sourcesFoot: Not used: Amwal Al Ghad's Thursday flow figures (they conflict with two other sources), AFP's October inflation figure, OneValor's undated $110.23 Brent quote, and a Rio Times preview that wrongly expected a hold. Pages that failed to open: CNBC's oil page (403). The Al Jazeera live blog was opened but gives no times or figures beyond the Riyadh interception. The reserves figures (7 October) and the 364-day T-bill auction (27 October) are the latest available and are labelled with their dates. items: The CBE raises rates by 100 bp to a 20% deposit rate, its first hike since March 2024, when most analysts expected a hold → the pound's slide past 56 and about $1.67 bn of foreign and Arab debt selling in three days (derived) push the CBE to defend the carry trade.

The Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, and markets largely price a December hike → elevated inflation and war-driven uncertainty keep US yields high (10-year 5.04%), narrowing the carry that holds foreign money in Egyptian bills.

EGX30 closes Thursday 0.64% higher at 49,596.14 while the EGX70 jumps 2.77% → local buyers absorb foreign selling (foreign institutions net sell EGP 229.1 mn on Wednesday), leaving the index about 2.85% lower over five sessions (derived).
Foreign and Arab net selling of Egyptian bills and bonds slows to $391 mn on Wednesday from $619.1 mn → debt outflows continue but ease as the pound holds at EGP 56.20 at the CBE.

Banque du Caire's retail book closes 27 times covered and the sale is upsized to 45%, with trading expected on 2 November → EGP 49.2 bn of retail orders chase EGP 1.8 bn of stock, showing local appetite for quality state assets even in a falling market.

EGP passes 56 per dollar at the CBE (sell 56.3511 on Monday) as foreign and Arab investors net sell about $664 mn of bills and bonds → secondary-market debt selling and regional risk drive the slide; importers lose, USD earners gain, and Thursday's CBE meeting is the test.

EGX30 closes Monday at 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions, and the FRA halves brokers' minimum liquid capital ratio to 5% → foreign selling and forced selling by leveraged holders prompt the regulator to ease the rule through Thursday.

Brent trades near $116 on Tuesday morning, about 55% above the $75 in Egypt's budget (derived) → Hormuz flows run at about 60% of normal and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia add supply fear, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Egypt's parliament backs military support for Saudi Arabia while the Houthis keep firing at Riyadh and the Eastern Province → a closer link to the regional war lifts Egypt's risk premium and puts Suez and tourism sentiment at risk.

The Fed decides today with a hold priced at about 93% after September's hike to 3.75–4.00% → a firm Fed keeps foreign holders of Egyptian bills under pressure and leaves the CBE no room to cut on Thursday.
EGP breaks 56 per dollar at the CBE for the first time → foreign sellers of T-bills (net $700.5 mn on Monday) are the driver; importers and leveraged names suffer, USD earners gain.
EGX30 falls 1.66% to 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions; EGX70 fell 11.07% on Sunday → liquidity, margin calls and foreign selling hit small caps hardest; Thursday's CBE meeting is the next test.

Parliament authorises Sisi to give military support to Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites → raises the regional risk premium on Egyptian assets and keeps Red Sea shipping risk alive for Suez revenue.
Brent sits at $115.41 while the US-Iran war keeps Hormuz under attack → Egypt's energy import bill and fuel subsidy gap widen just as the IMF's final review opens.

Banque du Caire prices its IPO at EGP 5.30 with the largest private tranche in EGX history → strong institutional demand helps the IMF divestment target but absorbs local liquidity before trading starts on 2 November.

stories.h: CBE surprises with a 100 bp hike, its first since March 2024
stories.src: AFP via Free Malaysia Today; Finimize (Reuters); El Balad; Cairo Mubasher
stories.what: The Monetary Policy Committee raises the overnight deposit rate to 20%, the lending rate to 21% and the main operation rate to 20.5%. A Reuters poll of 13 analysts expected a hold. The pound ends Thursday at 55.99 buy and 56.12 sell at the CBE, and El Balad describes the dollar as stable at banks after the decision.
stories.why: The CBE cites "challenging external conditions and elevated uncertainty" and wants to anchor inflation expectations. The pound hit a record low near 56 per dollar this week as foreign investors sold Egyptian debt.
stories.aff: T-bill yields, the carry trade, the pound, bank margins, borrowing costs for developers and leveraged companies, and the appeal of deposits against equities.
stories.eg: The deposit rate now sits about 6.1 points above September's 13.9% inflation (derived), a wider cushion to win back foreign holders of local debt.
stories.egx: Announced after Thursday's close, so Sunday is the first session to price it. Bullish for bank margins; bearish for developers, NBFIs and leveraged industrials.
stories.names: Banks (CIB, QNB Egypt, HDBK) bullish; developers (TMG, Palm Hills) and NBFIs bearish.

stories.h: EGX30 ends October 0.64% higher as small caps lead and breadth turns strongly positive
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Youm7; Cairo Mubasher; EnterpriseAM; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Thursday at 49,596.14, up 0.64%, after Wednesday's 1.64% fall. The EGX70 rises 2.77% to 16,779.72 and the EGX100 2.27% to 22,639.93. 180 stocks rise and 31 fall, and market cap gains about EGP 33 bn to EGP 3.892 tn. Beltone (+5.8%), AMOC (+4.9%) and Orascom Development (+3.7%) lead, while Abu Qir Fertilizers (-3.5%), Mopco (-2.5%) and Telecom Egypt (-1.7%) fall.
stories.why: None of the sources gives a single cause for the rise; the CBE's hike comes after the session. Flows are distorted by the Banque du Caire execution: foreign institutions net buy EGP 29.2 bn and Egyptian institutions net sell EGP 34.3 bn.
stories.aff: Small caps, brokers and the foreign-held blue chips that now face a higher rate environment.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 up 18.6% year to date even after this month's sell-off.
stories.egx: Neutral overall: broad gains but fertiliser names and Telecom Egypt lag, and the rate hike is not yet priced.
stories.names: Beltone, AMOC, Orascom Development (up); Abu Qir, Mopco, Telecom Egypt (down).

key.l: Banque du Caire offering executed on the EGX

stories.h: Banque du Caire's EGP 36.37 bn offering executes ahead of Monday's debut
stories.what: The public and private offering executes on the EGX for 6.862 bn shares, 45% of the bank's issued capital, at EGP 5.30 a share, worth EGP 36.371 bn. The private placement of about 6.519 bn shares is worth about EGP 34.55 bn and was six times covered. The shares start trading on Monday 2 November under the ticker BQDC, valuing the bank at about EGP 80.83 bn.
stories.why: The sale was raised to 45% from 30% with the Financial Regulatory Authority's approval, and the retail tranche was heavily oversubscribed.
stories.aff: Brokerages, sentiment toward state-bank listings, the privatisation programme and local liquidity.
stories.eg: A completed sale of this size counts toward Egypt's asset-sale goals as the IMF programme nears its end.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokerages; the debut tests demand above the offer price.

key.l: end date of Egypt's IMF programmes

stories.h: IMF aims for a staff-level deal on Egypt's final review before mid-December
stories.what: The IMF says its current mission aims to reach a staff-level agreement and take it to the Executive Board before mid-December. The programmes end on 15 December. Communications director Julie Kozack says talks focus on tight monetary policy and the fiscal consolidation plan, with structural reforms central.
stories.why: This is the final review of Egypt's current IMF programmes.
stories.aff: The last disbursements, Egypt's financing outlook, the pound and the state's divestment pace.
stories.eg: The CBE's hike on the same day matches the IMF's call to keep monetary policy tight.
stories.egx: Neutral to mildly bullish: a completed review would support the pound and foreign appetite for Egyptian assets.

stories.h: Brent slips to $114.88 on a Vance letter to Iran as Gulf attacks continue
stories.src: Reuters via The Globe and Mail; Khaleej Times
stories.what: Brent settles 44 cents lower at $114.88 and WTI 78 cents lower at $102.00, after both fell more than $2 during the day. US Vice President JD Vance reportedly writes to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei to revive talks, and Iran says it received the letter. A senior Iranian official rejects a new Qatari draft, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines near Hormuz.
stories.why: Hopes for diplomacy pull prices down, while Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and fears of a US strike on Iran after the 3 November midterms limit the fall.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel bill, the subsidy gap, global inflation, shipping costs and the pound.
stories.eg: Egypt imports most of its energy, and AFP notes high energy prices add to its economic strain.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers and energy-intensive industry; oil-linked names such as AMOC hold up better.
stories.names: Construction materials; consumer and food (bearish). AMOC (relative strength).

key.l: Houthi missiles shot down over Riyadh on Thursday

stories.h: Houthis fire at Riyadh again while Iran sets conditions for reopening Hormuz
stories.what: Saudi Arabia says it destroys two Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh, and earlier intercepts one aimed at the Eastern Province; one civilian is injured. Iran says it is discussing a plan with mediators to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but a senior official says it stays shut until its conditions are fully met. QatarEnergy buys US and other LNG to hedge against further disruption.
stories.why: The US-Iran war continues, with the Houthis extending attacks to Saudi Arabia.
stories.aff: Gulf energy infrastructure, shipping insurance, Red Sea traffic and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: AFP notes the war has pushed some shipping lines away from the Suez Canal, a key source of foreign currency.
stories.egx: Bearish for sentiment and tourism-linked names; no single EGX company is named.

stories.h: ECB holds but signals a December hike; US growth beats forecasts at 3.4%
stories.src: ECB; Reuters via Yahoo Finance; BEA
stories.what: The ECB keeps its deposit rate at 2.50%, its refinancing rate at 2.65% and its lending rate at 2.90%. Reuters sources call a 17 December hike all but certain, and Lagarde says a hike was debated. In the US, real GDP grows at a 3.4% annual rate in 3Q against 2.2% in 2Q, while PCE prices rise 2.1% and core PCE 2.5%.
stories.why: Rising energy costs push up inflation risks in Europe; US growth is led by investment and consumer spending.
stories.aff: Global bond yields, the dollar and the euro, and emerging-market carry trades.
stories.eg: Tighter policy in the US and Europe narrows the yield gap that draws foreign money to Egyptian bills.
stories.egx: Bearish for foreign-held blue chips through the carry channel.

stories.h: Egypt and the US discuss Sudan, Libya and maritime borders
stories.what: Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and Massad Boulos, Trump's senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, discuss Sudan on Wednesday, the ministry says on Thursday. Abdelatty calls for a comprehensive political settlement. They also discuss Libya and maritime boundary delimitation, without details.
stories.why: Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces have fought since April 2023, killing tens of thousands.
stories.aff: Egypt's southern border, refugee flows and regional diplomacy.
stories.eg: Stability in Sudan and Libya matters for Egypt's security and trade routes.
stories.egx: Neutral. No direct EGX channel is reported.

key.l: Prime Minister's decree behind the review

stories.h: Cabinet prepares higher fines for false news and tighter social media rules
stories.what: The Cabinet says it is preparing Penal Code amendments to raise fines for false news and rumours, as part of new digital safety rules. A committee recommends upgrading the NTRA's content unit with automated detection. The fine amounts and timetable are not set, and nothing is enacted yet.
stories.why: The government wants to regulate social media more closely.
stories.aff: Platforms, telecom operators and content creators.
stories.eg: Adds to the compliance load on digital businesses.
stories.egx: Neutral; no listed company is named.

week.event: Banque du Caire expected to start trading on the EGX
week.why: A test of demand above the EGP 5.30 offer price after an EGP 36.37 bn execution.
Oil traders fear a US strike on Iran after the vote; Brent is near $115.
Reuters sources call a hike all but certain, which would add to pressure on emerging-market carry.
The first inflation print after the CBE's 100 bp hike; September urban inflation was 13.9%. CAPMAS usually publishes around the 9th or 10th.
